caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 945 of 1999
lawyer:
Mr. Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan, Senior Advocate (Mr. K. S. Nabi, Advocate with him) Mr. Md. Aftab Hossain, Advocate-on-Record ------ for the petitioners. 
Mr. M. Enayatur Rahman, Advocate (appeared with the leave of the Court) instructed by Mr. A. K. Shahidul Huq, Advocate-on-Record ------- for the Respondent No.1. 
Respondents No.1-12: ------- Not represented.
parties:
Bangladesh Agricultural Development
Vs.
Giasuddin Ahmed and others
full_judgment:
Md. Ruhul Amin, J: This petition for leave to appeal by the respondent No.1- petitioner has been filed challenging legality of the judgment of 14th June, 1999 by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in Writ Petition No.4336 of 1997 making the Rule absolute directing the respondent No.1- petitioner to implement the order of the Ministry of Agriculture contained in Memo No.Krishi-5/Bibidh/41/90/10 dated 2nd February, 1991 within three months. By the aforesaid Memo Ministry of Agriculture directed the respondent No.1-petitioner to cancel the promotion of the respondent Nos.10 and 11 as General Manager and to inform the Ministry as to disposal of the case of promotion of the petitioner-respondent No.1 in accordance with law and as per Rules and Regulations. 

 2. Facts, in short, are that petitioner-respondent No.1 joined as Deputy Director in Bangladesh Agriculture Development Corporation (BADC) on 19th December 1967 and was promoted as Manager on 15th May, 1976. Respondent No.10 joined in BADC as Assistant Manager, a post equivalent to the post of Assistant Director, on 20th February, 1964 and was promoted to the post of Deputy Director and Manager on 20th May, 1968 and 15th May, 1976 respectively. Respondent No.11 joined BADC as Assistant Manager on 7th January, 1964 and was promoted to the post of Deputy Manager and Manager on 27 December, 1969 and 7th May, 1975 respectively. The petitioner-respondent No.1 and respondent No.10 though were promoted on the same day yet the petitioner-respondent No.1 was made senior to respondent No.10, as the petitioner-respondent No.1 was senior in the post of Deputy Director. It was mentioned in the letter of promotion in case petitioner-respondent No. 1 join in the post of Manager than the respondent No.10 would be reverted back to the post of Deputy Manager. The petitioner-respondent No.1 joined in the post of Manager on 20th May,1976. As in the meantime another post of Manager was created, the responded No.10 was not reverted back and that respondent No.11 was promoted to the post of Manager on 7th May, 1976 giving benefit of 2 years antedated seniority as freedom fighter, that even after that antedated seniority the petitioner-respondent No.1 was senior to the said respondent but the said fact was not considered in giving promotion to the respondent No.11. The petitioner-respondent No.1 submitted several representations but those were not considered by the BADC. Grading list of the Manager of BADC was prepared in 1990 and therein the petitioner-respondent No.1 was shown senior to respondent No.10 but junior to respondent No.11. The respondent No.11 was given current charge of General Manager but his performance being not satisfactory was reverted back to the post of Manager and thereupon petitioner-respondent No.1 was given current charge of General Manager (Supply). In due course BADC took step for regular promotion to the post of General Manager. There were 2 statutes - Bangladesh Agriculture Development Corporation Regulation Service Rules, 1967 and BADC Recruitment and Promotion Procedure, 1970. Matter of promotion of the employees governs by Recruitment Rules, but all on a sudden on 19th December, 1989 BADC took decision to introduce viva voce examination and circulated the said decision by the Memo Dated 28th  December, 1989 although no prior approval of the Government as required by Section 52 of BADC Corporation Ordinance, 1961 was obtained. Under the changed procedure petitioners-respondent Nos.1 and 3 others including respondent Nos.10 and 11 were called to appear before the Selection Board in viva voce examination and the respondent Nos.10 and 11 were promoted to the post of General Manager on 23rd April 1990. The petitioner-respondent No.1 represented to the Secretary Ministry of Agriculture for canceling the promotion to the post of General Manager since persons junior to him were promoted to the said post on the basis of viva voce examination for which no prior approval of the Government was taken. The Ministry of Agriculture by its Memo dated 2nd February, 1991 directed BADC to cancel the promotion of Respondent Nos.10 and 11 to the post of General Manager and to consider the case of promotion of the petitioner-respondent No.1 and to intimate compliance thereof. But BADC did not pay heed to the said direction of the Ministry of Agriculture. Ministry's direction having not been followed, 3 members committee was formed to give opinion as regard the promotion of the respondent Nos.10 and 11 and the committee gave its opinion for review of the promotions those were made on 12th April, 1990, 14th April, 1990 and 16th April, 1990. The petitioner-respondent No.1 was making representations to the Chairman of BADC, and to the Secretary, Ministry of Agriculture. Petitioner-respondent No.1's representations having not been considered he served a notice on 3rd July, 1997 demanding justice by way of impleading the order of Ministry of Agriculture dated 2nd February, 1991 and 10th June,1996 and the same was not replied. Thereupon petitioner-respondent No.1 filed the writ petition seeking direction on the respondent No.1-petitioner and others for the implementation of the directions as contained in the Memo dated 2nd February, 1991 and 10th June, 1996 of the Ministry of Agriculture. 

 4. The High Court Division made the Rule absolute upon observing that in the facts and circumstance of the case the petitioner-respondent No.1 is entitled to get the relief prayed for as the respondent Nos.10 and 11 were given promotion to the post of General Manager not in accordance with the Rules and Regulations of the Corporation and by suddenly changing the promotion procedure wherefore no approval was obtained from the Government. 

 5. Mr. Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan, learned Counsel appearing for the petitioner-respondent No.1 submits that the High Court Division was in error in holding that introduction of viva voce examination for the promotion of Officer of BADC to higher post required approval of the Government in as much as the learned Judges did not consider the distinction between the Regulations made under Section 52 of the Bangladesh Agriculture Development Corporation Ordinance, 1961 and Bangladesh Agricultural Recruitment and Promotion Procedure, 1970 in that former requires prior approval of the Government and the latter does not require such approval being not regulations and those are framed by the Board of Bangladesh Agricultural Development Corporation in exercise of the power conferred on it by the Ordinance. The matter of promotion of Respondent Nos.10 and 11 as well as others to the post of General Manager upon suddenly introducing viva voce examination without information to the Government was inquired into by a 3 Members Committee constituted the Ministry of Agriculture, the controlling Ministry of the BADC and the said committee made recommendation for review of the questioned promotion and thereupon Ministry directed BADC to review the promotion to the posts of General Manager already made and also the case of petitioner-respondent No.1 but BADC did nothing. The Ministry of Agriculture made known its disapproval more than once to BADC and that BADC was directed by the Ministry of Agriculture by its Memo dated 2nd February, 1991 to cancel promotion of respondent Nos.10 and 11 and to dispose of the case of promotion of the petitioner-respondent No.1 on compliance of the Rules and Regulations and to intimate the Ministry as to disposal of the matter of promotion of said respondent. The respondent No.1-petitioner in-spite of that did not finally consider the case of petitioner-respondent No.1 without offering justification therefor. It is seen from the materials on record that case of promotion to the post of General Manager was reviewed by a committee of 3 members and that the said committee submitted the report with the recommendation for review of the promotion made to the post of General Manager. Thereupon the Ministry of Agriculture though directed the BADC to review the case of promotion to the post of General Manager and that to dispose of the matter of promotion of the petitioner-respondent No.1 but still then BADC did nothing. The other contention of the learned Counsel that under the Ordinance in case of change in the Regulations made under section 52 of the Ordinance there is requirement of approval of Government but in case of change in Recruitment and Promotion Procedure framed by BADC approval was not necessary appears to be not well conceived one. The said contention if considered in the background of the repeated directions given by the Ministry of Agricultural to BADC to review the case of promotion of the petitioner-respondent No.1 in the light of the Rules and Regulations previous to the introduction of viva voce examination for promotion to the higher post clearly and manifestly show unsustainability of the submission of the learned Counsel of the respondent No.1- petitioner. As seen from the materials on record resorting to the sudden introduction of viva voce examination was not approved by the Ministry of Agriculture, the controlling Ministry of that BADC. The persistence of the BADC not to review their previous decision promoting respondent Nos.10 and 11 inspite of the directions of the Ministry at first by itself and thereafter in the background of the 3 members committee to cancel the promotion of the said two respondents and that non-disposing of the case of promotion of the petitioner-respondent No.1 in the light of the direction of the Ministry of Agriculture clearly indicates that in case of consideration of the case of the petitioner-respondent No.1 in due compliance of the Rules and Regulations his case of promotion would have preference over the case of promotion of the respondent Nos.10 and 11 or in other words sudden change in the procedure of promotion to the post of General Manager was made to give undue advantage to respondent Nos.10 and 11 upon depriving petitioner-respondent No.1 and because of that BADC was not complying with repeated directions of the Ministry of Agriculture as were in Memo dated 2nd February, 1991 and the subsequent Memos.
